children: Shares of Riot Platforms rose after its third-quarter earnings beat analyst forecasts, and the company said it has signed a new 15-year land lease.
Shares were 15% higher at $16.10 on Wednesday. The stock is up 27% year to date.
The bitcoin mining company and data center operator posted a third-quarter profit of $4.03 million, or 1 cent a share, compared with $104.5 million, or 26 cents a share, in the previous year.
Revenue rose 1% to $181.4 million, with data center revenue and engineering revenue offsetting lower bitcoin mining revenue.
Analysts polled by FactSet had expected per-share earnings at a loss of 36 cents on $160.8 million in revenue.

Chief Executive Jason Les said the company has signed a 15-year land lease with a Frontier AI lab, representing about $28 billion in contracted revenue over the initial term. Riot has contracted about $38 billion of data center revenue, and it expects to generate more than $2 billion of average annual net operating income at full deployment, he said.
